perspective:
Harold’s available information/from his perspective:

- He is Harold Padilla, a Project Manager. He feels frustrated and anxious because he believes his project team is unmotivated and this is hurting progress.
- He knows Arthur Begum as a police officer and friend, and he seeks Arthur’s advice at a local coffee shop.
- He tells Arthur his team seems unmotivated and he is at his wit’s end. He hears Arthur advise understanding each team member’s individual motivation, having one-on-one conversations, and making people feel valued and understood. Harold decides to try this and feels hopeful.
- He tells his team he wants one-on-one chats to understand their motivations. He hears Team Member 1 say it could be helpful, and Team Member 2 say they are open to it. He plans to schedule time with each person.
- After trying Arthur’s advice, Harold perceives that the team still is not responding well. He feels disappointed and worried and tells Arthur this.
- He hears Arthur suggest there may be deeper issues: personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold may need to dig deeper. Harold decides to set up more meetings.
- He feels determined and focused. He holds one-on-one meetings and asks team members about concerns.
- He hears Team Member 1 say there is tension between a few team members affecting work. He says he will look into resolving conflicts.
- He hears Team Member 2 say they feel overwhelmed by the workload and stressed, making motivation hard. Harold says he will see about redistributing tasks and that their well-being is important.
- He feels optimistic and empowered, believing addressing individual concerns will improve performance. He plans regular feedback sessions and team-building activities.
- He tells the team about these changes. He hears Team Member 1 say it sounds great and will help them work better together. He hears Team Member 2 agree and say it is good their concerns are being addressed. Harold says their input and well-being are crucial and urges them to make the project a success together.

He does not have access to other characters’ private thoughts, hidden events, or information beyond what he observed, heard, was told, or did himself.
